decisions.claim: B declined the invitation to join A and others at the concert this evening
decisions.reason: 'Why not?' presupposes B expressed a negative response or refusal to the invitation; 'declined' is a reasonable reading of this presupposition, though the exact firmness is uncertain.
decisions.counterexample: B might have merely expressed hesitation or asked a clarifying question rather than fully declining.

decisions.claim: B declined or gave a negative response to the invitation to join the concert
decisions.reason: c2 is a weaker, hedged version of c1 ('declined or gave a negative response' vs 'declined'). Both derive from the same presupposition in 'Why not?'; c1 is the more complete representative.

decisions.claim: B was invited to join a group going to a concert this evening
decisions.reason: Explicitly stated in Turn 1: 'Will you join us?' directly shows B was invited to join a group going to a concert this evening.

decisions.claim: B is not currently part of the group ('us') going to the concert
decisions.reason: 'Will you join us?' presupposes B is not currently part of 'us'; one cannot be asked to join a group one already belongs to.
decisions.counterexample: B could be peripherally associated with the group but not yet confirmed as going.
